1520|The compiler builds C → arm64 dylib right on the iPhone. It's a C compiler (TinyCC), not Objective-C, so you can't write [view setAlpha:0.5]. But every iOS class (UIKit, Foundation, AVFoundation and 90+ other frameworks) is available — you call them through the Objective-C runtime with the GX_MSG macros. gxkit.h isn't a replacement for UIKit, it's a bridge from C to any iOS class.

Frameworks to link are turned on in the “Libraries” menu. The core C frameworks have headers (CoreGraphics, CommonCrypto, CoreFoundation) — a normal #include. The rest (UIKit, AVFoundation, Security…) you call through GX_MSG, or declare the prototypes yourself.

gxkit.h — helpers for tweaks in C:

GX_CLS("UIView") — class
GX_SEL("setAlpha:") — selector
GX_MSG0(type, object, "selector")
GX_MSG1(type, object, "sel:", type1, arg1) … up to GX_MSG5
  example: GX_MSG1(void, view, "setAlpha:", CGFloat, 0.5);

gx_str("text") — NSString, gx_cstr(nsstr) — char*
gx_num_i/gx_num_d/gx_num_b — NSNumber; gx_int/gx_double/gx_bool — back to C
gx_alloc("UIView") — alloc+init; gx_prop(obj,"name") / gx_setprop(obj,"name",value) — properties by name (KVC)
gx_log("format %d", x) — to the system log (NSLog)
gx_alert("title", "message") — alert (on the main thread)
gx_main(fn, ctx), gx_main_after(sec, fn, ctx) — run on the main thread
gx_top_vc() — the app's top screen

gx_hook_method("Class", "sel:", 0, (IMP)my, (IMP*)&orig) — hook a method (1 — class method +)
gx_rebind("func", my, (void**)&orig) — hook a C function via its import
gx_image_base("UnityFramework") — load address of a library in memory

The finished .dylib appears next to the .c. To inject it into an app: app tools → “Inject dylib”.
